newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip with Bradys, no Eurobond impact.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip with Bradys, no Eurobond impact.

text.p: MinFin bonds eased on Thursday following the emerging market trend on fears of a U.S. interest rate rise, and dealers said news of the terms of Russia's second Eurobond having little impact on prices.
The two billion mark ($1.2 billion) seven-year nine-percent Eurobond was priced to yield 370 basis points over Bunds.
"The Eurobond turned out to have no impact on MinFins. The market is looking at U.S. Treasuries, which are not stable now," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.
MinFin bonds like Brady debt are heavily influenced by moves in the U.S. Treasury bond market. Emerging debt markets have been uneasy on fears of a U.S. interest rate hike later this month.

"Emerging markets are on the waiting side, fearing a rate hike. Many believe Eurobonds may be good news for the market, but there is no real momentum under the current trend," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said.
"Everything is going down, but without panic. Investors would not go into the market now to open new positions," he added.
Dealers said prices were likely to ease further as U.S.Treasuries slid on a 0.8-percent rise in February U.S. retail sales from an upwardly revised 1.5-percent gain in January.
